subject: Re: Safety telemetry sampling, escalation commitments & evidence
messages:
From: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@novabank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Safety telemetry: sampling rates, retention, and escalation lead times

Olga — thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our procurement review we need a concise set of commitments and evidence around the telemetry you collect for content-safety / abuse monitoring. Specifically: 
- event schemas (what fields are present for detection events)
- sampling behaviour (what fraction of requests are logged in full, and what gets redacted)
- retention windows (raw logs, aggregated metrics, alerts) and export options
- alerting/escalation SLAs (P1/P2 definitions, on-call rotation, expected response/ack times)
- evidence for historical incidents (redacted timeline + resolution steps)

Can you provide this as: (1) a short PDF we can attach to our RFP response and (2) an expected timeline for any contractual SLA language? We need this for NovaBank legal & InfoSec by next Friday (2027-05-28).

Best,
Alyssa
Security Program Manager
NovaBank

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@novabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety telemetry: sampling rates, retention, and escalation lead times

Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide a focused evidence bundle and proposed SLA language. Attached is a first-pass, the "Safety Telemetry Matrix" (PDF) that maps events -> schema -> retention -> redaction rules.

High-level notes:
- We log structured detection events for any model request that triggers a policy match or model-confidence threshold. Non-triggering requests are captured as aggregated metrics by default; raw request logs for non-triggering traffic are sampled at 0.1% unless the customer opts into full logging.
- PII redaction: keys we consider sensitive (payment data, SSNs, raw card PANs) are redacted at capture time via token-level filters and deterministic hashing.
- Retention: raw logs (triggering events) default 90 days; aggregated metrics 2 years. Longer retention or export via S3/GCS can be contractual.
- Escalations: our standard enterprise incident SLA is 4 hours to acknowledge P1, 1 business day for complete root cause ETA. We can tighten these in contract up to a 1-hour ack for an SLA addendum.

I'm looping in Ben for contractual terms and Marcus (cc'd separately) for schema examples and sample event JSON. Can we schedule a 30-min working session tomorrow to align on what NovaBank needs in the RFP bundle?

Attachment: redwood_safety_telemetry_matrix_v2.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@novabank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety telemetry: sampling rates, retention, and escalation lead times

Alyssa / Olga — Marcus here (Infra / Safety instrumentation). A few technical clarifications and an attached sample event schema: 

1) Event schema (attached sample_event_schema.json): top-level fields include: event_id, timestamp, model_id, model_version, request_id, user_id (hashed), input_token_count, matched_policy_ids, match_scores, action_taken (block/allow/flag), kv_cache_snapshot (if relevant), and redaction_flags.

2) Sampling behaviour: 
   - Default: full capture for policy-triggering requests (100% of triggering events).
   - Non-triggering traffic: probabilistic sampling set to 0.1% for raw text capture; we also keep non-triggering counters at 100% (aggregates per model/route/minute).
   - Customer-controlled sampling: we can increase sampling for specific routes, user cohorts, or by random seed for time-boxed investigations.

3) Redaction rules (implementation): deterministic token hashing for PII fields, configurable field-level redaction in the schema. We store a redaction audit log (who changed rules, when).

4) Alerts & Escalation hooks: alerts are emitted to customer-configurable channels (webhook, PagerDuty, email). For enterprise customers we provide a dedicated webhook payload (see sample schema) and a secondary on-call rotation that includes a Redwood safety engineer during business hours.

Attachment: sample_event_schema.json (JSON)

Happy to jump into a working session and walk through the schema in detail. If you have a particular retention/PII requirement we can propose the config changes and produce contract language.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@novabank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety telemetry: sampling rates, retention, and escalation lead times

Thanks — the materials look promising. A couple of follow-ups before we present to InfoSec: 
- We need a clear commitment for maximum storage of raw user content for non-triggering requests: is 0.1% hard-cap unless contractually changed? Would you consent to a default contract clause that caps sampled non-triggering raw content at 0.5%?
- For P1/P2 definitions, can you provide your internal definitions (e.g., P1 = production availability impact + escalatory abuse vector) so our risk team can map to NovaBank categories?
- For alerts: does Redwood support automatic suppression/dedup windows (to avoid alert storms) and can you provide sample webhook payloads (we saw JSON but would like example with redacted fields)?

Finally — can you include a short redacted timeline of a prior safety incident (customer name redacted) that shows detection -> alert -> investigation -> mitigation -> postmortem (no identifying customer content, just timestamps and actions)? That helps legal sign-off.

Alyssa

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@novabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Safety telemetry: sampling rates, retention, and escalation lead times

Alyssa — quick update and proposed mutual action plan so we hit your 2027-05-28 deadline: 

Mutual action plan (summary):
- By 2027-05-20: Redwood delivers: (A) redacted incident timeline (PDF), (B) exported sample webhook payload, (C) updated telemetry matrix with default contractual caps (attached xlsx).
- By 2027-05-24: NovaBank reviews and provides any counter-requests on retention or SLA tightening.
- By 2027-05-26: Joint working session to finalize SLA language (30 min).
- By 2027-05-28: Delivery of final evidence bundle for your legal & InfoSec.

Short answers to your bullet points: 
- Sampling default: 0.1% non-triggering capture is the product default and is enforced at the service layer; we can accept a contractual default cap of 0.5% with explicit opt-outs requiring customer consent. We'll put suggested clause language in the SLA workbook.
- P1/P2 definitions: attached workbook includes our recommended definitions and response windows; P1 = confirmed abuse leading to operational or reputational harm (ack within 1 hour, mitigation ETA within 4 hours). P2 = suspected abuse with limited scope (ack within 4 hours, mitigation ETA within 1 business day).
- Alert suppression: yes — we support deduplication windows and adaptive suppression based on rule fingerprinting. We will include a sample redacted payload and schema.

Attachments: incident_escalation_sla_commitments.xlsx (XLSX)

Can we schedule the 30-min session tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT? Ben will be available for contract-level questions; Marcus will be on the call for the schema.

Best,
Olga
